synth.name: espeak
synth.note: D8 (DR-0017) as amended by DR-0041: eSpeak NG at NVDA's default rate, rate boost off. NVDA's default eSpeak NG rate on a fresh configuration is 30 on NVDA's 0-100 scale: the driver sets rate 30 in __init__ (NVDA release-2026.2 source/synthDrivers/espeak.py:216) and SynthDriver.initSettings keeps a driver's own initial values on first load (source/synthDriverHandler.py:365-385); rate boost defaults to off (espeak.py:388). The nvda.ini committed in M1 must not set an eSpeak rate. The effective rate is recorded from the running synth each run (EnvManifest.synth.rate).

nvda.note: Pinned by the @guidepup/guidepup 0.35.0 manifest (guidepup/nvda 0.2.1-2026.2). NVDA Remote Access relay: TLS on 127.0.0.1:6837, channel guidepup. The relay certificate in this build is valid 2026-06-28 to 2027-06-28, which bounds the shelf life of this exact pin.

scream.note: SHA-256 computed by Claude on 2026-10-02 from the GitHub release download; GitHub publishes no digest for this 2020 release, so this is trust on first use. In M1a, before the certificate is added to TrustedPublisher, the driver's Authenticode signature status (Get-AuthenticodeSignature), signer and issuer are recorded alongside the signer certificate thumbprint (DR-0012 D3, amended by DR-0040). If the chain is valid and the signer is consistent with the release, the thumbprint is pinned; if the certificate is self-signed, authenticity rests on trust on first use and the owner is asked first. The schema refuses a pinned thumbprint until the signature status, signer and issuer are pinned.
